transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yeah, thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I guess I'm here because, well, for a long time now I've been walking around with this sort of... I don't know, flat, heavy feeling? 

I mean, I really don't want to make a big deal out of it or sound ungrateful, because work is going okay and everyone is really nice to me. I shouldn't complain. I just... I still feel a bit down and kind of empty most days, even when things are fine. 

Is that... does that make sense for why I'd come here? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
How long have you been feeling this way most days?

Um, well... I guess it's been a while. Maybe around two years and two months? Give or take? 

It kind of started right around the time I finished this big dashboard project at work. It ended up putting me in the spotlight a bit, which—I mean, it was a really good thing! I was super grateful for the opportunity and the recognition, I really was. But ever since then, I've just had this... lingering feeling. 

I tried to just push past it, because I know I should be happy about how my job is going and I didn't want to seem unappreciative. Is it okay that I waited this long to come in? I really hope I'm not wasting your time with something that started that far back.
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you've lost interest in activities you once liked?

Um, well... I guess I still do some of the things I used to do. Like, I still go to the movies with my friends sometimes, and I try to keep up with my reading when I can. I mean, they're still fine, you know? 

Maybe I don't get quite as... excited about them as I used to? But I think that's normal, right? Getting older and having more responsibilities at work, it makes sense that you wouldn't have as much energy for hobbies. I really try to stay engaged and be a good friend when we go out. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just don't want to make it sound worse than it is.
Can you describe what your mood is like on most days? Do you feel down or hopeless most of the time, even when things seem to be going okay?

Um, well... I guess I wouldn't say I feel down all the time, exactly. Like I said, things are okay at work, and I try really hard to keep a positive attitude about it. I don't want to sound like I'm complaining. 

But... maybe there is a little bit of, um, I don't know if "hopeless" is the right word, but... well, I used to be really driven. Like, I had all these plans mapped out for getting my MBA and the next steps in my career as an analyst. And I was really excited about them! But lately... I don't know, I look at those same plans and I just kind of assume I'm not going to get there. Like, no matter how much effort I put in, it just won't happen. 

I'm sure it's just a phase, though, you know? Everyone gets a little discouraged sometimes. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound too dramatic.
Would you say that most days, you feel this low or empty mood, even if it's not extremely intense?

Um, yeah... I guess that's a pretty good way to describe it. It's not like I'm crying all the time or anything like that. I really do try to keep a smile on my face, especially at work. 

But... yeah, I think I'd say that most days, there's just this... flat, kind of heavy feeling? Like, even when things are going perfectly fine at the office, or when people are being really nice to me, I still just feel sort of down. Or empty, I guess. It's actually why I finally decided to come in, to be honest. I just couldn't shake it. 

I know it probably sounds like I'm making a big deal out of nothing, since it's not super intense, but... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed yourself doing things more slowly, or feeling like it's harder to get motivated to do even small tasks?

Um, well... I don't think so? I mean, I still get all my reports done on time at work, and I try really hard to stay on top of things. I wouldn't want my boss to think I'm slacking off or anything. 

I guess sometimes getting started on a project takes a little more effort than it used to, but I think everyone procrastinates a bit, right? I definitely don't feel like I'm moving in slow motion or anything like that. I still get up and get dressed and go to work every day. I hope that's okay? I just wouldn't say I'm moving slower, really.
Have you found yourself feeling like you're not good enough, or that you're failing even when you're doing your best?

Um, well... I mean, I really try to do a good job. I don't want to sound like I'm fishing for compliments or anything, but my team is usually pretty happy with my work. 

But... I guess, sometimes, I do have these thoughts. Like... well, I built this dashboard for my department a while ago, and people still bring it up and say nice things about it. And I know I should just say thank you, but... my first thought is always that I somehow just fooled them into thinking it's good, or that I just got lucky. 

And then, if I miss a follow-up or send an email a little late... it feels like, I don't know, like it's proof that I'm not actually as capable as everyone thinks I am. That they're finally going to realize I'm not good enough. 

I know it's probably silly to think that way, and I really try not to let it affect my work. I hope it doesn't make me sound incompetent? I just... yeah, I guess I do feel like I'm failing sometimes, even when I'm trying my hardest. Is that normal to feel that way?
Have you noticed that you feel tired or that you don’t have much energy, even when you haven’t done anything physically or mentally exhausting?

Um, well... I try to stay as active as I can. I mean, I'm only 22, so I feel like I should have plenty of energy, right? I don't want to sound lazy or anything. I really do try to push through it.

But... I guess, yeah, I have been feeling pretty tired lately. It's just... by the afternoon, I'm just so wiped out. Even when it's been a totally normal day, not super stressful or anything. Just doing simple things, like fixing a spreadsheet error or finishing up some expense paperwork... it feels like it takes everything I have. 

And I usually play soccer, but lately, just getting myself to go feels like... I don't know, like I'm dragging my body and my brain through mud. I still go most of the time, because I don't want to let my team down, but it's just really hard. 

I know everyone gets tired after work, so maybe I'm just not managing my time well or something? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just complaining about normal stuff. Is it okay that I feel that way?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately—like eating more or less than usual, or gaining or losing weight without trying?

Um, well... I don't think so? I mean, I try to eat pretty healthy, you know? I wouldn't want to let myself go or anything. I still make sure to have all my meals and everything. 

I guess maybe I'm not always super hungry, but I think that's just because I sit at a desk most of the day, right? So I don't need as much food. I definitely haven't noticed any major weight changes, my clothes all still fit the same. I try to stay on top of that kind of thing. 

I hope that's the right answer? I just... I haven't really been paying super close attention to it, but I'm pretty sure everything is normal there. Is it bad if I haven't noticed a change?
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more often, even when it's not really your fault?

Um, no, I don't think I do that. I mean, I always make sure to take responsibility if I actually mess something up, you know? I definitely don't want to sound like I'm the type of person who just passes the blame to other people. If I make a mistake on a project or something, I own up to it right away. 

But... if it's genuinely not my fault, like if another department just didn't send me the data I needed on time, I don't really sit around feeling guilty about it. I try to just be logical and focus on fixing the problem instead. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound cold or anything? I just... I don't think I feel guilty unless I actually did something wrong. Does that answer your question okay?
Have you ever found yourself thinking about death or dying, or wished you were dead, even just briefly?

Um, no. No, definitely not. I mean, I know things have been a little tough lately with feeling tired and all, but I would never think about anything like that. I really value my life, you know? I'm only 22, I have my whole career ahead of me, and I wouldn't want to do anything to mess that up. 

I know some people get to that point when they're stressed, and I totally get that, but I'm really not like that. I try to stay as positive as I can. Even when work is overwhelming or I'm feeling drained, I just try to push through it and look on the bright side. 

I hope you don't think I'm the kind of person who would just give up like that? I promise I'm really trying my best to handle everything. That's a good thing, right? That I don't have those kinds of thoughts?
Have you found that activities you used to enjoy, like playing soccer or reading, don't bring you the same sense of pleasure or satisfaction anymore?

Um, well... I mean, I still do those things. I still go to soccer on weekends, and I always make sure to finish the books I start. I really don't want to be someone who just quits all their hobbies, you know? I think it's important to stay active and keep your mind sharp. 

I guess... maybe sometimes it feels a little more like a routine than it used to? Like, I'm just going through the motions a bit? But I think that's just because work has been so busy lately, and I'm tired. It's totally normal to not be super excited about running around on a field when you've been working hard all week, right? 

I still participate, though! I definitely don't let my team down or anything. I just... maybe I don't get that huge rush of excitement from it right now. But I'm still doing it all, I promise. That's what matters most, isn't it? Just keeping up with everything?
Have you noticed that activities you used to really enjoy, like playing soccer or reading, now feel like chores or don’t give you any real satisfaction, even when you finish them?

Um, I think... well, like I was kind of trying to say just a minute ago, I definitely wouldn't call them chores. That makes it sound like I'm complaining about having to do them, and I really try not to be a complainer! I mean, when I finish a tough book, I still feel good about getting through it. It's an accomplishment, you know? 

I guess it's just that the excitement isn't quite as loud right now, mostly just because I'm so focused on staying on top of my job and I get a little worn out. But I definitely don't feel like my hobbies are a burden or anything like that. I'm really trying my best to stay well-rounded and keep up with normal life. 

I hope I'm explaining that right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture, since I know we kind of just touched on this. Am I making sense?
Even though you still do the things you used to enjoy, like reading or playing soccer, do you find that they don’t bring you any real happiness or satisfaction anymore?

Um, well... I feel like we're kind of circling the same thing, and I really want to make sure I'm giving you the answer you're looking for. I just... I wouldn't say they don't bring me *any* happiness. That sounds so... empty, I guess? 

I mean, I still smile when my team scores a goal, and I still like the feeling of closing a book when I'm done. It's just... maybe it's a little quieter right now? Like, I'm just a bit too tired to jump up and down about it. But I definitely still get something out of it. I wouldn't keep doing them if I was totally miserable, you know? 

I really am trying to stay positive and engaged with everything. I hope that's okay? Like, it's normal to have phases where things are just a little less exciting, right? I just don't want you to think I'm completely shutting down or anything, because I'm really not.
Would you say that your low or empty mood is present most of the day, nearly every day, even if it's not extremely strong?

Um, well... I guess I wouldn't call it empty, exactly. That sounds a bit dramatic, doesn't it? I just... I came in because, for a while now, I've just had this kind of flat, heavy feeling. 

Even when things at work are going okay, or people are being really nice to me, I still just feel a bit down most days. Not, like, crying all the time or anything like that! Just... a little heavy. 

I try really hard not to let it show, and I'm still getting my work done and everything. I just wanted to see if maybe there was a way to feel a bit lighter? I hope that makes sense. Is it normal to feel like that sometimes, even when things are technically fine?
Even when you finish a book or play a full game of soccer, do you find that you don't really feel any joy or satisfaction from it anymore?

Um, I'm sorry, I feel like I'm maybe not explaining myself very well today, since we keep coming back to this. I really don't mean to be difficult or confusing! 

I... I definitely still feel something. Like I said, I still like the feeling of finishing a book, and I still like playing soccer. I really do. It's not like I'm totally numb to it all. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just going through the motions like a robot or something. 

I guess it's just... I'm a little tired lately, so maybe the joy isn't as intense as it used to be? But it's definitely still there. I really try to appreciate the good things, you know? I hope I'm giving you the right answer this time. I just don't want to make it sound worse than it actually is.

Can you recall a time in the past when reading a good book or playing soccer gave you a clear sense of joy or excitement, and would you say that feeling is noticeably less now, even if you still do those things?

Um, yeah, I guess I can remember when it felt a little different. Like, maybe a couple of years ago, I'd get really, really into a book and stay up way too late reading it, or I'd be super pumped for a soccer game all week. 

And, um, I guess maybe it is a little less intense now? Like I said, it's just a bit quieter. But I really don't think it's a huge problem or anything! People change, right? As you get older and start working and stuff, you just don't have the same energy to get super excited about every little thing. That's pretty normal for someone my age, isn't it? 

I just want to make sure I'm not overstating things. I still really enjoy my hobbies, I promise. I just... maybe I'm just a little more mellow about them now? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for.
Would you say that reading or playing soccer don’t feel as rewarding or enjoyable as they used to, even though you still do them?

Um, I mean, I guess we kind of just talked about that, right? I'm sorry, I don't want to sound like a broken record, I just... I really want to make sure I'm answering you correctly. 

I don't think it's that they aren't rewarding anymore. I still like doing them! I really do. It's just... maybe it's just the tiredness I mentioned? Like, I'm working a lot now, and I'm just a bit drained by the time I get around to my hobbies. 

So it's not that the activities themselves are less enjoyable, it's just that I'm, you know, a bit more worn out when I do them. That makes sense, doesn't it? I just really don't want you to think I'm sitting around feeling sorry for myself or not trying to enjoy life. I'm definitely still trying! Is that... is that okay to say?
Would you say that reading a good book or playing soccer no longer feels pleasurable, even though you still do them?

Um, I... I feel like we're sort of stuck on this, and I'm really sorry if I'm frustrating you. I know you've asked this a few times now, and I really want to be helpful. 

But no, I wouldn't say they aren't pleasurable anymore. That sounds so... so absolute, you know? Like I'm just completely miserable or something, and I'm really not! I still get pleasure from them. I just... I guess I'm just a normal guy who gets a little tired from working all week, and maybe that takes the edge off the fun sometimes. 

I'm really trying to be honest with you, I promise. I just don't want to agree to something that makes me sound like I've totally given up on things I like. I hope you understand what I mean? I'm really trying my best to give you the information you need.
